arxiv-1708-04717.title: Observing FRB 121102 with VERITAS; Searching for Associated TeV Emission
arxiv-1708-04717.creator: for the VERITAS Collaboration
arxiv-1708-04717.description: Abstract Fast radio bursts are bright, unresolved and short flashes of radio emission originating from outside the Milky Way. The origin of these mysterious outbursts is unknown, but their high luminosity and short duration has prompted much speculation. The discovery that FRB 121102 repeats has enabled multiwavelength follow up, which has identified the host galaxy.

arxiv-2111-09834.title: Error estimation for the time to a threshold value in evolutionary partial differential equations
arxiv-2111-09834.creator: Jehanzeb H. Chaudhry, Donald Estep, Trevor Giannini, Zachary Stevens, Simon J. Tavener
arxiv-2111-09834.description: Abstract We develop an a posteriori error analysis for a numerical estimate of the time at which a functional of the solution to a partial differential equation (PDE) first achieves a threshold value on a given time interval. This quantity of interest (QoI) differs from classical QoIs which are modeled as bounded linear (or nonlinear) functionals of the solution.

arxiv-2211-14097.title: Bayesian variance change point detection with credible sets
arxiv-2211-14097.creator: Lorenzo Cappello, Oscar Hernan Madrid Padilla
arxiv-2211-14097.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel Bayesian approach to detect changes in the variance of a Gaussian sequence model, focusing on quantifying the uncertainty in the change point locations and providing a scalable algorithm for inference. We do that by framing the problem as a product of multiple single changes in the scale parameter.

arxiv-2401-09771.description: Abstract Bubble curtains are widely used for sound mitigation during offshore pile driving to protect marine life. However, the lack of well validated hydrodynamic models is a major factor in the inability to predict the sound attenuation of a bubble curtain a priori .

arxiv-2508-12201.title: A mathematical model of HPAI transmission between dairy cattle and wild birds with environmental effects
arxiv-2508-12201.creator: H.O. Fatoyinbo, P. Tiwari, P.O. Olanipekun, I. Ghosh
arxiv-2508-12201.description: Abstract Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), especially the H5N1 strain, remains a major threat to animal health, food security, and public health. Recent spillover events in dairy cattle in the United States, linked to wild birds, highlight the critical importance of understanding transmission pathways at the cattle–wild bird–environment interface.

arxiv-2510-05112.description: Abstract . Pipeline parallelism is an essential distributed parallelism method. Increasingly complex and diverse DNN models necessitate meticulously customized pipeline schedules for performance. However, existing practices typically rely on predefined schedules, each with strengths, but fail to adapt automatically to the emerging model architectures. Exploring novel high-efficiency schedules is daunting due to the enormous and varying schedule space.

arxiv-2510-14943.title: LaSeR: Reinforcement Learning with Last-Token Self-Rewarding
arxiv-2510-14943.creator: Wenkai Yang, Weijie Liu, Ruobing Xie, Yiju Guo, Lulu Wu, Saiyong Yang, Yankai Lin
arxiv-2510-14943.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has recently emerged as a core paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). To address the lack of verification signals at test time, prior studies incorporate the training of model’s self-verification capability into the standard RLVR process, thereby unifying reasoning and verification capabilities within a single LLM.

arxiv-2512-20793.title: Higher-Dimensional Information Lattice: Quantum State Characterization through Inclusion-Exclusion Local Information
arxiv-2512-20793.creator: Ian Matthias Flór, Claudia Artiaco, Thomas Klein Kvorning, Jens H. Bardarson
arxiv-2512-20793.description: Abstract We generalize the information lattice, originally defined for one-dimensional open-boundary chains, to characterize quantum many body states in higher-dimensional geometries. In one dimension, the information lattice provides a position- and scale-resolved decomposition of von Neumann information. Its generalization is nontrivial because overlapping subsystems can form loops, allowing multiple regions to encode the same information.

pmc-10596809.creator: K Thompson, J Qi, A Pham, E Viviani
pmc-10596809.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the importance of tailored preparedness plans to cope with potential disease outbreaks. During the pandemic, a major challenge for policymakers was finding the balance between containing the disease and supporting mental health and well-being. Although COVID-19 lockdowns and accompanying restrictions mitigated the spread of the virus, many countries witnessed significant increasing rate of depression during these periods.

pmc-10733194.title: Regulation of lipolysis by 14-3-3 proteins on human adipocyte lipid droplets
pmc-10733194.creator: Qin Yang, Zinger Yang Loureiro, Anand Desai, Tiffany DeSouza, Kaida Li, Hui Wang, Sarah M Nicoloro, Javier Solivan-Rivera, Silvia Corvera, Christian Metallo
pmc-10733194.description: Adipocyte lipid droplets (LDs) play a crucial role in systemic lipid metabolism by storing and releasing lipids to meet the organism's energy needs. Hormonal signals such as catecholamines and insulin act on adipocyte LDs, and impaired responsiveness to these signals can lead to uncontrolled lipolysis, lipotoxicity, and metabolic disease.

pmc-11308904.title: Demographic and geographic distribution of diabetes and pre-diabetes risk in rural settings: results from a cross-sectional, countywide rural health survey in Sullivan County, New York
pmc-11308904.creator: David C Lee, Leah Ross, Carolina Quintero Arias, Melissa Rony, Rahi Patel, Erica Jensen, Robert Petcu, Daniel Imas, Brian Elbel, Lorna E Thorpe, Rebecca Anthopolos
pmc-11308904.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-11457844.title: Clinical cell-surface targets in metastatic and primary solid cancers
pmc-11457844.creator: Marina N. Sharifi, Yue Shi, Matthew R. Chrostek, S. Carson Callahan, Tianfu Shang, Tracy J. Berg, Kyle T. Helzer, Matthew L. Bootsma, Martin Sjöström, Andreas Josefsson, Felix Y. Feng, Laura B. Huffman, Chris Schulte, Grace C. Blitzer, Quaovi H. Sodji, Zachary S. Morris, Vincent T. Ma, Labros Meimet
pmc-11457844.description: Therapies against cell-surface targets (CSTs) represent an emerging treatment class in solid malignancies. However, high-throughput investigations of CST expression across cancer types have been reliant on data sets of mostly primary tumors, despite therapeutic use most commonly in metastatic disease. We identified a total of 818 clinical trials of CST therapies with 78 CSTs.

pmc-11534242.title: Adaptation of the G-NORM (Gender norms scale) in Uganda: An examination of how gender norms are associated with reproductive health decision-making
pmc-11534242.creator: Erica Sedlander, Rachel Granovsky, Catherine Birabwa, Dinah Amongin, Ronald Wasswa, Nadia Diamond-Smith, Peter Waiswa, Kelsey Holt, Jeffrey B. Bingenheimer
pmc-11534242.description: BackgroundRestrictive gender norms exacerbate health inequalities all over the world. More specifically, they prevent women from seeking preventive health services, constrain women’s economic empowerment, and are associated with reproductive health decision making. Gender norms, a subset of social norms, are dynamic and change over time.

pmc-11570736.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Take Home MessageThe aim of our study is to assess whether flexible ureteroscopy with a suction bendable ureteral access sheath is comparable to mini-percutaneous nephrolithotomy in terms of the stone-free rate and perioperative outcomes.Keywords: Urolithiasis, Retrograde intrarenal surgery, Ureteral access sheath, Percutaneous nephrolithotomy, Flexible urteroscopy, Tip bandable suction ureteral access sheath

Background

According to the European Association of Urology and American Urological Association guidelines, percutaneous nephrolithomy (PCNL) is the preferred treatment option for renal stones larger than 2 cm [1], [2].

pmc-11641184.title: Coumarin Derivative Hybrids: Novel Dual Inhibitors Targeting Acetylcholinesterase and Monoamine Oxidases for Alzheimer’s Therapy
pmc-11641184.creator: Teresa Żołek, Rosa Purgatorio, Łukasz Kłopotowski, Marco Catto, Kinga Ostrowska, Giulio Vistoli
pmc-11641184.description: Multi-target-directed ligands (MTDLs) represent a promising frontier in tackling the complexity of multifactorial pathologies like Alzheimer’s disease (AD). The synergistic inhibition of MAO-B, MAO-A, and AChE is believed to enhance treatment efficacy. A novel coumarin-based molecule substituted with O-phenylpiperazine via three- and four-carbon linkers at the 5- and 7-positions, has been identified as an effective MTDL against AD.

pmc-11642439.title: Alpha-Synuclein and Microglia in Parkinson’s Disease: From Pathogenesis to Therapeutic Prospects
pmc-11642439.creator: Hyemi Eo, Sehwan Kim, Un Ju Jung, Sang Ryong Kim, Leonardo Roever
pmc-11642439.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by both motor symptoms and non-motor features. A hallmark of PD is the misfolding and accumulation of alpha-synuclein (α-syn), which triggers neuroinflammation and drives neurodegeneration. Microglia, brain cells that play a central role in neuroinflammatory responses and help clear various unnecessary molecules within the brain, thus maintaining the brain’s internal environment, respond to α-syn through mechanisms involving inflammation, propagation, and clearance.

pmc-11660237.title: Ankle Ligament Reconstruction-Return to Sport After Injury (ALR-RSI) Scale and Return to Sports After Ankle Ligament Reconstruction or Repair – A Systematic Review
pmc-11660237.creator: YuChia Wang, Maximilian Hinz, Wyatt H. Buchalter, Amelia H. Drumm, Emre A. Eren, C. Thomas Thomas Haytmanek, Jonathon D. Backus
pmc-11660237.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Category:Ankle; SportsIntroduction/Purpose:While objective outcome measures assessing foot and ankle function are well established to determine return to sport (RTS) following ankle injuries, psychological factors have been recognized in recent years to be equally important. The Return to Sport after Injury (RSI) scale has become an emergingly useful tool used in assessing psychological readiness to return to sporting activity after various pathologies and their treatment.

pmc-11714703.title: Dynamic contrast enhanced MRI reveals impaired blood brain barrier in basal forebrain region in patients with Alzheimers disease: A pilot study
pmc-11714703.creator: Ondrej Lerch, David Kala, Zuzana Nedelska, Haris Hadzic, Jakub Otahal, Jakub Hort
pmc-11714703.description: BackgroundBlood brain barrier (BBB) is a protective layer of cells that separates the circulatory system from the brain. Its dysfunction is one of the possible mechanisms leading to onset of Alzheimer's disease (AD), a progressive neurodegenerative disease and a leading cause of dementia worldwide.

pmc-12476820.title: HOX and MEINOX in cellular plasticity, fibrosis, and cancer
pmc-12476820.creator: Mustafa Keleş, Aysen Gunel-Ozcan
pmc-12476820.description: HOX transcription factors and their cofactors, MEINOX, are critical regulators of positional identity and cellular plasticity. While their functions are essential during embryonic development, they also play key roles in maintaining adult tissue homeostasis. Dysregulation of HOX and MEINOX has been implicated in the pathogenesis of various diseases, including fibrosis and cancer.

pmc-12547694.title: Anal cancer screening and the role of clinicians providing gynecologic care: A survey of anal cancer screening knowledge and practice patterns at an urban tertiary medical center in the United States
pmc-12547694.creator: Colin B. Russell, Nicholas S. Raja, Gabriela Ashenafi, Arshpreet Kaur Mallhi, Natalie A. Saunders, Elizabeth J. Campbell, Hope K. Haefner, Kathryn C. Welch
pmc-12547694.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveThis study aims to assess the current knowledge of anal cancer, screening, and practice patterns among clinicians providing gynecologic care.MethodsIn January 2024, 207 clinicians providing care for adults at an urban tertiary medical center (the University of Michigan Hospitals, Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States) received a 14-question electronic survey regarding their knowledge of anal cancer, screening practices, and desire to learn more about anal cancer screening. Descriptive statistics were used to present findings.ResultsThe final analyses included 121 respondents.

pmc-12563090.title: Health Literacy and Medication Adherence Among Low-Income Older Adults in the Inner Center of Portugal: A Questionnaire-Based Study
pmc-12563090.creator: Carla Perpétuo, Ana I. Plácido, Alexandra Monteiro, Ramona Mateos-Campos, Maria Teresa Herdeiro, Fátima Roque
pmc-12563090.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Introduction: Health literacy (HL) is a key determinant of health outcomes, particularly among vulnerable populations such as low-income older adults. Limited HL is associated with poor understanding of medication instructions and lower medication adherence, which can compromise therapeutic success. This study aims to assess the levels of HL and medication adherence among low-income older adults and to analyse the relationship between HL, medication adherence, and other determinants.

pmc-13336550.title: Motivation and pleasure deficits reflect altered network embedding of normal brain deviations in schizophrenia☆
pmc-13336550.creator: Jacob Holker, Aaron Clouse, Sierra Ann J Gilday, Jacob Jensen, Delaina Cimmino, Barrett Humble, Jacob Johnston, Kennedy Madrid, Madeleine Reading, Sam Johnson, Braydon Lee, Stefan Ehrlich, Matthew J Smith, Lei Wang, Derin Cobia
pmc-13336550.description: Background:Negative symptoms in schizophrenia are associated with significantly worse outcomes, and their factor structure (i.e., diminished motivation and pleasure [MAP] and diminished expressivity [EXP]) has only recently been clarified. Studies investigating structural imaging correlates of negative symptoms have largely focused on cortical regions involved in motivation, reward processing, affect expression, and language.

pmc-13543938.title: Stretching a doublet into a triplet for FLT3 AML
pmc-13543938.creator: Keith W. Pratz
pmc-13543938.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). y is currently enrolling to examine the clinical utility of the triplet approach combining AZA, VEN, and GILT vs the standard doublet approach of AZA/VEN for the treatment of patients with FLT3-ITD AML (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06317649).
